item.title: 100X AI Cultures: Can AI turn 10x Engineers into 100x Engineers?
item.description: As AI reshapes work, which organizations can turn increasingly accessible intelligence into greater productivity? Counterpoint Global’s updated AI Beneficiaries research introduces the AI Productivity Spread, a new Culture Quant metric offering insight into organizational adaptability and potential value creation.

item.title: Video: Real Rates Take the Lead
item.description: The recent global bond selloff was driven by a sharp rise in real yields, while widening dispersion across credit, securitized and emerging markets created a more selective opportunity set. Utkarsh Sharma explores what drove the shift, how fixed income sectors responded and why quality, carry and active security selection remain central as policy tightens and volatility rises. Watch this video to find out more.

item.title: September Market Recap
item.description: On September 16, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) unanimously voted 12-0 to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00%, aspersistent, above-target inflation outweighed risks to the labor market.

item.title: Private Credit Market Monitor - Q3 2026
item.description: Timely insights on the private credit landscape, exploring the trends, market developments, and investment considerations shaping the asset class.

item.title: Physical AI: From Tokens to Torque
item.description: As AI moves into the physical economy, the investment universe expands beyond models and semiconductors to the component, manufacturing ecosystem and adapters that enable it. Samson Hung and Freddie Cai examine how emerging markets are benefiting from strengths in manufacturing, robotics and technology adoption.

item.title: The Rise of French Bond Yields: Is a European Contagion Ahead?
item.description: In this edition of Caron’s Corner I’m joined by Umar Malik of the Portfolio Solutions Group to discuss the significant rise in French bond yields and its potential impact on the rest of Europe.

item.title: Filling the Gap: The Expanding Role of Direct Lenders in Europe
item.description: Mark Jochims explores why European direct lending has its own distinct set of borrowers, structures, and dynamics.

item.title: Real Rates Take the Lead
item.description: Global bond markets repriced sharply in September as major central banks raised interest rates and real yields drove most of the selloff. Higher-quality credit remained relatively resilient, while lower-rated debt faced greater pressure. The Broad Markets Fixed Income team highlights the growing importance of income, relative value, and active security selection in a more volatile market environment.

item.description: Overview of the current landscape across equity markets.

item.description: In-depth review of fundamentals and valuations across emerging markets debt.

item.title: Why the Lower Middle Market Matters
item.description: Discover why many investors view the lower middle market as an attractive area of private equity, supported by favorable supply-demand dynamics, attractive valuations, and significant value-creation potential.

item.title: Municipal Bond Market Monitor – Q3 2026
item.description: Overview of the trends and developments in the muni bond markets.

item.title: Video: Mapping Europe's Barbell
item.description: Europe is in the midst of a major policy shift, driven by spending on defense, energy and advanced manufacturing. In this Big Picture video, Jitania Kandhari breaks down what the reordering of priorities means for the continent, country by country, theme by theme.

item.title: High Yield Market Monitor – Q3 2026
item.description: An in-depth review of the US and European High Yield markets.

item.title: Floating-Rate Loan Market Monitor – Q3 2026
item.description: Insight on loan market fundamentals and the role of floating-rate loans within portfolios.

item.title: The BEAT™ for Q4 2026 - October
item.description: Use The BEAT™ as your timely resource for the markets. Each edition gives you ideas and insights that show you how to navigate the current investment environment.

item.title: The Case for Asian Equities
item.description: For the past decade, global equity portfolios have been dominated by U.S. companies that produced strong earnings growth and shareholder returns. But active investing is not about past winners, but identifying positive returns that are not yet reflected in current prices. Amay Hattangadi and Steve Sun make the case that Asia is where those returns now sit.

item.title: Delivering Specialized Solutions at Scale
item.description: Institutional allocators are consolidating around fewer, broader partners. Ben Huneke and Rui de Figueiredo discuss how specialization, platform breadth, and true customization are shaping what large institutions expect from an asset manager today.

item.title: Equity Market Commentary - September 2026
item.description: In his most recent TAKE, Senior Portfolio Manager Andrew Slimmon encourages investors to focus on the micro, company results, as equities respond to the new more restrictive Fed policy, particularly once we move past mid-term elections. He also shares what is behind the positive change in non-US investing.

item.title: Quantum Computing Revisited
item.description: Advances in quantum error correction are moving the industry closer to fault-tolerant computing. Counterpoint Global examines what has changed, the hurdles that remain and where commercial value may ultimately emerge.

item.title: Mapping a Warming World: The Rise of Climate and Geospatial Intelligence
item.description: Physical climate risk is now a balance-sheet issue: 2025 natural catastrophes caused ~$220bn in economic losses, under half insured. A new intelligence layer is emerging across satellites, sensors and climate models, but cheaper hardware and proliferating open datasets are commoditising generic data and forecasts. 1GT argues durable advantage lies with firms pairing hard-to-replicate proprietary data with differentiated models, embedded in customer workflows with measurable ROI.

item.title: Higher Yields Are a Headwind, Not a Stop Sign
item.description: Higher yields don’t have to end the risk rally, because why yields are rising matters. The stronger cashflows generated from very high nominal growth rate - a whopping 6.5% - wins over higher yields that pressure valuations lower.

item.title: Why Private Equity? A Core Growth Engine in Today's Portfolio
item.description: Private equity is one of the main ways investors gain exposure to privately held companies. It has historically delivered better long-term risk-adjusted returns than public equity, achieving this primarily by making operational improvements across portfolio companies, with the aim of growing revenues and expanding margins.

item.title: Video: A Firmer Fed
item.description: A firmer Fed, flatter yield curves and sharper dispersion are reshaping global fixed income. Leon Grenyer explains why income remains compelling—but selectivity is now more important than ever. Watch this video to find out more.

item.title: A New Era for Middle Market Private Equity: Five Imperatives for an Evolving Market
item.description: The tailwinds that supported private equity returns for much of the past decade are fading. In a market defined by higher financing costs, increased competition, the impact of AI, slower liquidity, and greater performance dispersion, we believe five capabilities may increasingly separate PE managers from the pack.

item.title: Mapping Europe's Barbell
item.description: Europe is undergoing its most significant economic policy shift since the creation of the euro. After decades in which economic policy prioritized fiscal restraint, globalization and market efficiency, eurozone governments are prioritizing economic security, strategic autonomy and industrial resilience. This is more than merely increased public spending. Capital is being reallocated to defense, energy and digital infrastructure, advanced manufacturing and critical technologies.

item.title: A Firmer Fed
item.description: August markets were shaped by a more hawkish Federal Reserve, flatter yield curves, and strong performance across spread sectors. Emerging market debt, high yield bonds, and leveraged loans outperformed, while investment grade credit remained stable. The Broad Markets team discusses where they see opportunities across global fixed income markets amid tight valuations and rising policy uncertainty.

item.title: To Free or Not to Free (Cash Flow)
item.description: Free cash flow (FCF) is central to evaluating large technology companies, especially the hyperscalers, where surging investments have squeezed FCF. We define FCF, show where each company stands on results and forecasts, and ask if heavy investment has shifted them in the life cycle. Returns on the marginal dollar invested have varied widely. We link FCF to ROIC: negative FCF is fine provided ROIC exceeds the cost of capital. We end with how consensus estimates for key value drivers have changed.

item.title: September FOMC Meeting - Three Minute Recap
item.description: Kendal Cehanowicz, Portfolio Manager, Morgan Stanley Global Liquidity, discusses the latest messaging from the Federal Reserve about monetary policy and the implications for short-term investors.

item.title: Private Markets Perspectives Q3 Webinar
item.description: In this quarter's webinar, our investment leaders provided an update on the signals observed in the latest private markets data, a summary of the latest private markets asset class views, and a deep dive into private markets secondaries, including sources of growth, evolving structures, and techniques for navigating competition.

item.title: Cyber Risk in U.S. Water Systems: A Municipal Credit Perspective
item.description: Recent cyberattacks on water and wastewater utilities highlight growing vulnerabilities in essential public infrastructure. While disruptions have been limited, the incidents underscore the importance of operational resilience, cybersecurity investment, and preparedness. The article explores how cyber risk influences municipal credit analysis and long-term financial stability.

item.title: Video: What it takes for consumer brands to win in an AI era
item.description: In this video we explore how greater transparency, shifting consumer behaviour and AI are changing the consumer industry — and what this means for brand power, value and long-term investment opportunities. Watch to find out more.

item.title: Strategic Income: An All-Weather, Multi-Sector Approach
item.description: Strategic Income is an all-weather, multi-sector fixed income strategy. Andrew Szczurowski and Chip Driscoll discuss its “plus sector” roots, flexibility and portfolio role. Watch this video to find out more.

item.title: Structural Drivers Propel U.S. Industrial’s Next Growth Wave
item.description: In a macro environment characterized by higher growth, higher interest rates and divergent demand drivers, investors need to target industries and real assets which take advantage of pockets outsized growth. This growth will likely be closely aligned to long-term thematics including AI capex, manufacturing reshoring, and higher defense spending.

item.title: Expanding the Investor Toolkit: A Modern Introduction to Alternatives
item.description: Alternative investments are no longer reserved for institutional investors. Learn how private equity, private credit, real assets and hedge funds can help investors diversify portfolios and access new sources of return.

item.title: Public to Private Equity in the United States: A Long-Term Look
item.description: Institutional investors have shifted their allocations in U.S. equities from public to private markets over the past 40 years, causing reverberations for investors, executives, and policymakers. We examine key trends in public and private equity, specifically buyouts and venture capital. We review their size, M&A patterns, and returns. A lot has changed since we wrote about this in 2020, including the end of “easy money,” tougher exits, increased access to capital, and surging capital needs.

item.title: The Atomic Steppe
item.description: Today, nuclear power is witnessing a major renaissance driven by increased electricity demand to power AI and renewed focus on energy security. About 100 new nuclear plants are currently planned, nearly matching the total number built worldwide over the last 20 years. Paul Psaila and Sebastian Schafer explore the nuclear revival and why Kazakhstan is well positioned to benefit.

item.title: Is It Still Worth Getting on a Plane? Field Notes from Recent Research Trips
item.description: Information is everywhere, but insight is not. From commuter drones in China and semiconductor bottlenecks in Europe to industrials in the U.S., recent research trips have helped the International Equity Team test investment theses, assess management quality and deepen their understanding of shifting industry dynamics. In an age of AI and instant information, the team explores why in-person research and human judgement still matter.

item.title: Equity Market Commentary - August 2026
item.description: In his most recent TAKE, Senior Portfolio Manager Andrew Slimmon reminds investors to think beyond the macro. Instead, he encourages a focus on the micro, specifically the extraordinary Q1 results delivered so far that are forcing analysts to raise future earnings estimates.

item.title: European Real Estate Credit: Safety Amid Fluid Backdrop
item.description: Europe's economy has held up despite higher energy prices, geopolitical risk and fragmentation, though rate policy has turned hawkish and base rates are higher. Real estate debt still screens attractively against alternatives: values have repriced ~25%, income is durable in structurally aligned sectors, and new supply is scarce as construction costs rise. MSREI remains constructive, but diversification, dynamic allocation and stock-picking assets that fit new occupier demand remain critical.

item.title: Evaluating Crypto ETPs: Fees, Custody and Benchmarks
item.description: As crypto exchange-traded products continue to gain adoption, investors may want to look beyond traditional investment considerations. Understanding factors such as custody arrangements, sponsor experience, liquidity and benchmark methodology can help provide a more complete framework for evaluating crypto ETPs.

item.title: The Maturity Transformation of U.S. Treasury Debt and What it Means for Asset Allocations
item.description: Treasury buybacks have the potential to be a net positive for equities and ease financial conditions that are broadly supportive of financial assets. We discuss how this policy action impacts our asset allocations.

item.title: Video: Selectivity Takes the Lead
item.description: With carry still attractive but valuations tight, we highlight where active management may uncover opportunities across duration, emerging markets debt, corporate credit and securitized assets. Watch this video to find out more.

item.title: Why the Real Estate Matters in Net Lease Investing
item.description: Elevated market volatility and a resilient economy favor net lease investments that are characterized by durable, long-term cashflows with fixed escalations in sectors and assets that are supported by long-term structural demand drivers. However, given heightened credit risk with some tenants who may struggle to absorb higher input costs it is critical that investors truly understand the residual value of the underlying real estate in addition to the credit of the tenant in assessing the attractiveness of a net lease investment.

item.title: Selectivity Takes the Lead
item.description: July marked a shift from the relative stability of June toward renewed pressure from higher global yields. Fixed income markets remained functional, supported by technical demand, but rising rates, tight spreads, and growing dispersion reinforced the importance of carry, relative value, and active security selection.

item.title: Direct Lending: Selective Exposure
item.description: Private credit has entered a new phase. Stronger underwriting, wider spreads and greater manager differentiation are reshaping the direct lending market, creating new opportunities for institutional investors focused on income and portfolio resilience.

item.title: Beyond Wires: How Investors Can Turn the Great Grid Upgrade into the Next Multi-Decade Investment Opportunity
item.description: This paper argues that the "Great Grid Upgrade" will be driven not only by building new grid infrastructure but by deploying a ‘toolkit’ of commercially-proven, mature technologies that improve grid flexibility, capacity, stability, and visibility. Deploying and integrating these solutions, will better allow operators to continue to deliver affordable power reliably in a market experiencing broad-based demand growth for the first time in a generation.

item.title: A Higher Nominal Growth World Brings on Higher Volatility
item.description: A shift is occurring toward a higher nominal growth environment, evolving Fed communication strategies, and implications for both bond and equity markets. Volatility may rise as a result, we discuss how we are managing our asset allocation in this new regime.

item.title: When It Seems There Is Only One Game in Town
item.description: A narrow AI-driven rally is reshaping global markets, with a small group of stocks accounting for a growing share of returns. While supported by strong earnings, this concentration raises questions about sustainability and valuation. What does this mean for long-term investors? The International Equity Team explores the risks of crowding, the durability of AI-driven profits and the opportunities emerging beyond the current market leaders.

item.title: Real Estate Midyear Outlook: Constructive Amid Fluid Backdrop
item.description: The current macroenvironment remains resilient despite elevated volatility and divergence across markets. As inflation and energy prices keep central banks hawkish, real estate continues to offer attractive relative value, supported by a 25% repricing, durable income streams, and constrained supply. In this environment, diversified portfolios and selective asset-level investing remain critical.

item.title: The Wisdom of Crowds in Markets: Crowd Behavior in Prediction, Betting, and Stock Markets
item.description: We review the wisdom of crowds in the context of prediction markets, sports betting markets, parimutuel betting markets, and the stock market. For each, we describe the market, give a history, examine its accuracy, see how it aggregates information, check for diversity breakdowns, and consider the role of incentives. The betting markets are zero-sum, but the stock market has positive expected returns. Understanding how markets work is useful for evaluating opportunities for excess returns.

item.title: The MSIM Quantitative Duration Strategy Model: A Factor-Based Approach to Managing Interest Rates
item.description: Anton Heese and Matas Vala explore the Quantitative Duration Strategy Model, one of the proprietary tools the team uses to enhance their investment process, as it helps provide structure and rigour with identifying and processing relevant and important data.

item.title: From Electric Vehicles to Humanoids: China’s Next Manufacturing Leap
item.description: Humanoid robots sit at the intersection of hardware, AI, manufacturing, real-world data and customer integration. Longer-term value may depend more on intelligence, software and fleet learning. Jerry Pang and Rose Kim examine how China’s humanoid robots are beginning to move from televised spectacles to manufacturing and commercial roles.

item.title: Private Credit Market Monitor - Q2 2026
item.description: Timely insights on the private credit landscape, exploring the trends, market developments, and investment considerations shaping the asset class.

item.title: 2026 Russell Reconstitution: A New Lens on Growth, Value and Active Management
item.description: The 2026 Russell Reconstitution highlights a broader shift in today’s market: the traditional lines between Growth and Value are becoming less distinct. Learn what Eaton Vance investment teams think that means for portfolio construction, diversification and where they see opportunities for active investors.

item.title: July Market Recap
item.description: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 9-3 to maintain the federal funds rate at its target range of 3.50%-3.75%, marking the fifth consecutive meeting without a policy change.

item.title: Building Durable Real Estate Portfolios at Morgan Stanley with Lauren Hochfelder
item.description: Lauren Hochfelder, Head of Global Real Assets, recently joined the Capital Allocators podcast to share the experiences that shaped her path — from navigating the Global Financial Crisis to the thematic approach behind her team's strategy today. A candid look at how one of the industry's most experienced voices thinks about durable portfolio construction, and where she sees opportunity and risk ahead.

item.title: Broad Markets Fixed Income Multi-Sector Playbook: A World of Increasing Dispersion
item.description: What should fixed income investors be watching for the rest of 2026? The Broad Markets Fixed Income team explores the key issues.

item.description: Kendal Cehanowicz, Portfolio Manager, Morgan Stanley Global Liquidity, discusses the latest messaging from the Federal Reserve about monetary policy and the implications for short-term investors.

item.title: Video: Built on Resilience
item.description: Watch our latest fixed income video update for a concise look at how markets navigated June’s challenges, why demand for income continues to support credit and securitized sectors, and where we see opportunities as valuations remain tight and dispersion rises.

item.title: Three Blockchains. Three ETPs. One Framework
item.description: A plain-language framework explaining Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana—what each network is designed to do, how they differ and why those differences may matter to investors.

item.title: Staking Fundamentals: Earning Rewards by Securing a Network
item.description: A plain-language overview of crypto staking—how it works, why it matters, and how it can shape investor outcomes, including through exchange-traded products.

item.title: Solana Fundamentals: Scale, Speed and Smart Contracts Insight
item.description: Explore how Solana’s high‑speed blockchain architecture, use of smart contracts and role as digital infrastructure distinguish it from other digital assets.

item.title: Looking Ahead: Rate Uncertainty and Innovation
item.description: Elevated inflation, heightened geopolitical and economic volatility, and rapidly evolving technologies continue to present both opportunities and challenges. This brief update covers six key themes likely to remain in the headlines and shape your strategic thinking throughout the remainder of the year.

item.title: Ethereum Fundamentals: Smart Contracts, Decentralization and Financial Applications
item.description: Explore how Ethereum’s programmable blockchain, smart contract capabilities and role in decentralized finance shape its position among digital assets.

item.title: Lauren Hochfelder on The Alts Report
item.description: In this episode of The Alts Report, Brian Holzer sits down with Lauren Hochfelder, Head of Global Real Assets at Morgan Stanley Investment Management, to discuss triple net lease investing, including how these investments are structured, what distinguishes them from more traditional commercial real estate strategies and where they may fit within a diversified portfolio.

item.title: An Introduction to Private Equity Co-Investing
item.description: Private equity co-investing has become central to private markets, allowing investors to allocate directly into deals alongside private equity funds. Here, we discuss what co-investing is, how it works and how it fits within a private equity portfolio.

item.title: There’s a New Sheriff in Town: Culture Change at the Fed
item.description: Fed policy is changing and may reshape how we think about valuations, inflation and interest rate policy. The Fed may also increase their supply-side data indicators versus what have traditionally been demand-side. We explain the relevance and nuances of these changes.

item.title: OPPORTUNITY NOW: Autonomous Mobility Is Imminent, Are You Ready?
item.description: China’s autonomous mobility market offers a compelling long-term growth opportunity, supported by large demand, cost advantages, strong technology and improving unit economics. Learn why Global Opportunity has conviction in this emerging theme.

item.title: The BEAT Video - Q3 2026
item.description: In The BEAT for Q3 2026 we highlighted five important themes, amongst others, that we see across the global investment landscape.

item.title: Infrastructure 2026 Midyear Outlook
item.description: We are currently observing a structural reorganization within established megatrends. In data centers, compute is shifting from a centralized model to a distributed, multi-layered network, as inference-driven and latency-sensitive workloads scale. This expands demand and reshapes where and how infrastructure is deployed.

item.title: Private Equity 2026 Midyear Outlook
item.description: The foundation for a multi-year recovery is now in place. The next phase depends less on direction than on breadth.

item.title: Hedge Funds 2026 Midyear Outlook
item.description: As markets grow more complex and the dispersion of outcomes increases, we believe hedge funds will continue to play a valuable role in investor portfolios through 2026, offering the potential to enhance returns, reduce volatility, and provide diversification regardless of the market’s ultimate direction.

item.title: Real Estate 2026 Midyear Outlook
item.description: Performance is increasingly driven by structural growth drivers rather than cyclical market exposure. Secular themes such as AI, deglobalization, demographic shifts and energy demand are creating clear winners and laggards. This environment reinforces the importance of selectivity, diversification and active capital allocation to capture emerging pockets of outperformance.

item.title: 2025 Stewardship Report
item.description: Calvert's engagement team discusses engagement & proxy voting activities that aim to drive positive change on financially material sustainability topics.

item.title: Private Credit 2026 Midyear Outlook
item.description: We believe the current market environment is becoming more favorable for scaled private credit lenders as pricing power improves and financing demand accelerates, driven by cyclical and secular forces.

item.title: Built on Resilience
item.description: Fixed income markets showed resilience in June as persistent inflation and cautious central banks reinforced expectations for restrictive policy. Strong demand, lower rate volatility and investor appetite for income supported credit, securitized and emerging market debt, while tight valuations point to carry and security selection as key return drivers.

item.description: A sharp reversal from 2025 and a compelling setup for what's next.

item.description: Quality stocks have lagged in recent years, but history suggests durable businesses with strong fundamentals remain well positioned to create long-term shareholder value.

item.description: Morgan Stanley’s International Equity team discusses how exchanges have evolved into critical financial infrastructure, with resilient revenues and growing roles in data, clearing and market activity.

item.title: Bright Prospects Podcast: Episode 3
item.description: Fresh from his annual research trip to China, Global Stars PM Alex Gabriele joins Portfolio Specialist Sarah Hudson for episode 3 of the Bright Prospects podcast to share what he saw on the ground - including the EV-filled streets of Shanghai and robotics businesses moving from prototypes to real-world deployment - as he sought to uncover the next generation of exciting growth companies trading at compelling valuations.

item.title: Video: Ten Investment Truths About Artificial Intelligence
item.description: In this Big Picture video, Jitania Kandhari covers ten investment truths about AI: from the extraordinary speed of the infrastructure buildout, to the rise of autonomous agents, to the two competing architectures that will shape the geopolitical order for decades.

item.title: Mid-Year Equity Market Outlook - July 2026
item.description: In his latest TAKE, Senior Portfolio Manager Andrew Slimmon shares his mid-year equity market outlook, explaining why the 2026 rally looks rational and where opportunities may emerge beyond the obvious AI beneficiaries.

item.title: Markets in Motion
item.description: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) unanimously voted to maintain the federal funds rate at its target range of 3.50%-3.75%.

item.title: The Blurred Lines Between Growth and Value Create an Investment Opportunity
item.description: Growth and Value managers are overlapping more now than they have in the past … and may not provide the desired diversification. Equity strategist Chris Morahan joins me to discuss investment opportunities across the Growth and Value styles.

item.title: Opportunistic Credit: Flexible Capital for an Evolving Market
item.description: Discover why opportunistic credit is gaining momentum as borrowers seek flexible capital solutions and investors seek differentiated returns in the evolving private markets.

item.title: Terms of Trade: The Quiet Tailwind Behind Emerging Market’s Comeback
item.description: A common thread across emerging markets is an improvement in their terms of trade, which is helping to strengthen external balances, support currencies and improve the earnings outlook for domestically-oriented sectors. Paul Psaila and Uday Tharar explain.

item.title: Video: Risk Assets Persist
item.description: Strong demand, record issuance and resilient fundamentals helped keep global fixed income markets constructive in May—but tight valuations and rising dispersion mean selectivity remains key. Watch this video to find out more.

item.title: Opportunities and Expectations: The Present Value of Growth Opportunities in Valuation
item.description: Stock prices reflect the value of current earnings and the option to make investments that create value, the present value of growth opportunities (PVGO). We analyze how PVGO as a percentage of price serves as a measure of market timing and find it has some use. Next, we observe that the stocks of companies with low PVGO percentages outperformed those with high percentages. Lastly, a simple analysis suggests the PVGO percentage provided a higher return than the value factor in recent years.

item.description: In today's complex macro environment, active fixed income management offers institutional investors both stability and return potential.
